questions.question:
다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
English has become a widely used "lingua franca" due to its extensive usage and adoption in many countries, allowing individuals who speak different native languages to communicate and understand each other. About 1.75 billion people around the world use English as a useful means of communication, due to the high demand of English in critical fields such as science, technology, business, and entertainment. Moreover, in the digital era, people are exposed to a vast amount of online information and resources in English on a daily basis. These factors have consistently contributed to the widespread use and global influence of the English language.
choices: ① The Difficulty of Learning English as a Second Language
② What Makes English a Global Lingua Franca
③ How Science and Technology Depend on English
④ The History of the English Language in Britain
⑤ Why Digital Media Prefers the English Language
questions.explanation: 영어가 광범위한 사용·약 17.5억 사용자·여러 핵심 분야의 수요·디지털 노출 등으로 세계 공통어가 된 요인을 설명하므로 ②가 제목으로 적절하다. 나머지는 본문의 일부 소재이거나 본문에 없는 내용이다.  [출처: 교과서 3과 / 공통영어1]
questions._orig: English as a Global Language 단락

questions.question:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것을 고르시오.
The machine doesn't simply follow human orders but learns by itself, ① <u>which</u> is done through a branch of machine learning called deep learning. ② <u>Enabled</u> by this process, a machine can discover distinct patterns from numerous data. Moreover, AI can even learn established art styles only to avoid them. Just as major artists such as Picasso and Van Gogh once ③ <u>did</u>, AI trains itself by mimicking other styles until it creates its own. Not only ④ <u>it imitates</u> existing works, but it also generates something entirely new. What makes this remarkable is ⑤ <u>that</u> the results are largely beyond human control.
choices: ① which
② Enabled
③ did
④ it imitates
⑤ that
questions.explanation: 부정어구 Not only가 문장 앞에 오면 주어와 (조)동사가 도치되어야 하므로 ④ "it imitates"는 "does it imitate"가 되어야 한다. 따라서 ④. ②는 분사구문의 수동(Enabled), ③은 대동사(did), ⑤는 보어절 접속사(that)로 모두 어법상 옳다.  [출처: 교과서 4과 / 공통영어1]
questions._orig: AI creativity mechanism 단락

questions.question:
밑줄 친 <u>just as photography eventually came to be seen as art rather than technology more than a century ago</u>가 다음 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
This question is unresolved, but more and more art critics see AI-generated artworks as a new field of art, <u>just as photography eventually came to be seen as art rather than technology more than a century ago</u>. In 2018, a portrait created by AI was sold for nearly half a million dollars, helping AI artworks become more accepted in the traditional art world.
choices: ① a new medium initially dismissed as mere technique can later win recognition as a true art form
② technology and art have always been regarded as completely separate domains
③ photography lost its artistic value once newer technologies appeared
④ only traditional forms of art can be truly appreciated over time
⑤ artworks become valuable mainly when they are sold at high prices
questions.explanation: 밑줄은 사진이 한때 기술로 여겨지다 마침내 예술로 인정받은 역사를 들어, AI 아트도 새로운 예술 분야로 인정받을 수 있음을 비유한 것이다. 따라서 ①. ②④는 본문과 반대, ③⑤는 왜곡·초점 이탈이다.  [출처: 교과서 4과 / 공통영어1]
questions._orig: AI art photography 비유 단락

questions.question:
다음 글을 읽고 답할 수 없는 것은?
When a language is adopted in a specific region, it is natural for it to undergo changes as the local people utilize it to reflect their daily realities. The change is particularly noticeable in vocabulary. In Indian English, the term "prepone" was coined to mean "to reschedule" as the opposite of "postpone." For instance, if a meeting scheduled for Thursday is moved to Wednesday, it is considered "preponed." Hong Kong English speakers shout "add oil" to show encouragement, a direct translation from a Chinese expression, which originally meant to inject more gasoline into an engine. In the Philippines, there are many houses with "dirty kitchens," which are not actually "dirty" kitchens. Instead, they refer to kitchens outside the home, where most of the cooking takes place to avoid trapping heat and smell inside the house in a hot climate.
choices: ① What does the Indian English word "prepone" mean?
② In which country do people use the expression "add oil"?
③ What was the original meaning of the expression "add oil"?
④ Why are "dirty kitchens" in the Philippines located outside the home?
⑤ How many new English words has India added to the dictionary?
questions.explanation: 본문은 prepone의 의미(①), add oil 사용 지역(②)과 원래 뜻(③), 필리핀 dirty kitchen이 집 밖에 있는 이유(④)를 설명하지만, 인도가 사전에 추가한 단어의 수는 언급하지 않으므로 ⑤는 답할 수 없다.  [출처: 교과서 3과 / 공통영어1]
questions._orig: English Evolves to Fit Local Realities 단락

questions.question:
다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
There are several issues when we conceive of the philosophy of art. One issue is raised by the question: what is art? Most commonly, one attempts to resolve it by providing a definition, which attempts to identify the essential nature of art, or at least principles of classification for distinguishing art from nonart. Traditionally it searches for characteristics that all artworks share and all nonartworks lack. The conception of art has a neat answer: something is art if it is made to create significant aesthetic value. However, this answer has carried less and less conviction as art has developed through the twentieth and twenty-first centuries. We have countless examples of items put forward as art that aim for something other than artistic satisfaction: pop art replicas of soup cans, lint scattered across a gallery floor, and so on. Some of these works may have an aesthetic value, but appreciation of them requires much contextual understanding. The seemingly strange turns art has taken over the recent past is an important reason why the concept of art should be reformed.
choices: ① Aesthetic Value: The Only True Measure of Art
② Why the Traditional Definition of Art Needs Reform
③ How Pop Art Destroyed Classical Beauty
④ The Essential Nature Shared by All Artworks
⑤ Distinguishing Art from Nonart Made Simple
questions.explanation: 미적 가치라는 전통적 예술 정의가 20~21세기 예술 발전으로 설득력을 잃었고, 예술 개념이 개혁되어야 한다는 글이므로 ②가 제목으로 적절하다. 전통적 정의를 옹호하는 선지들은 본문이 반박하는 입장이다.  [출처: 절대유형 15강 22번]

questions.question:
다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
We are fascinated by neuroscientists' findings about our powers of thinking and imagination. But as the great naturalist philosopher David Hume knew, nature is too strong in us, and it will not let us abandon our cherished and familiar ways of thinking for long. Hume knew that however curious an idea and vision of ourselves we entertained in our study, or in the lab, when we returned to the world to dine and make merry with our friends, our most natural beliefs and habits returned and banished our stranger thoughts and doubts. It is likely that whatever we have learned about the error of our thinking and about the fictions we maintain, they will remain ______ in our everyday lives.
choices: ① an obstacle to true happiness
② a source of constant doubt
③ easily abandoned over time
④ irrelevant to our natural beliefs
⑤ the dominant guiding force
questions.explanation: Hume는 우리의 가장 자연스러운 믿음과 습관이 낯선 생각을 몰아낸다고 보았으므로, 사고 오류를 알더라도 그 자연스러운 믿음이 일상에서 지배적 안내자로 남을 것이라는 ⑤가 적절하다.  [출처: 절대유형 21강 22번]
questions._orig: We are fascinated by neuroscientists' findings about our powers of thinking and imagination, our abilities to represent and report our thoughts, and we wonder at them and about their applications to ourselves. But as the great naturalist philosopher David Hume knew, nature is too strong in us, and it will not let us abandon our cherished and familiar ways of thinking for long. Hume knew that however curious an idea and vision of ourselves we entertained in our study, or in the lab, when we returned to the world to dine and make merry with our friends, our most natural beliefs and habits returned and banished our stranger thoughts and doubts. It is likely that whatever we have learned and whatever we know about the error of our thinking and about the fictions we maintain, they will remain the dominant guiding force in our everyday lives.

questions.question:
글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳을 고르시오.
[주어진 문장] It is important, however, that the subject be unaware that he is being observed.

One strategy for studying behavior is to observe and record events as they naturally occur in life. ( ① ) Researchers utilizing this method, called naturalistic observation, do not bring their subjects into the laboratory and manipulate their behavior in any way. ( ② ) Nor do they choose groups of subjects or create different experimental conditions. ( ③ ) Naturalistic observation is commonly used to study animal behavior, such as the hibernation habits of bears or the maternal behavior of hens. ( ④ ) For example, a psychologist using naturalistic observation to study how children of various races play together would watch groups of children playing in the school yards or parks, but he would remain at a distance so as not to be detected. ( ⑤ ) If the children noticed that a strange adult was watching, they might behave differently than they otherwise would.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '관찰 대상이 관찰되고 있음을 몰라야 한다'는 내용이다. 거리를 두고 들키지 않게 관찰한다는 예시(④ 뒤) 앞에 와야 자연스러우므로 ④에 들어간다.  [출처: 절대유형 12강 23번]
questions._orig: One strategy for studying behavior is to observe and record events as they naturally occur in life. Researchers utilizing this method, called naturalistic observation, do not bring their subjects into the laboratory and manipulate their behavior in any way. Nor do they choose groups of subjects or create different experimental conditions. Naturalistic observation is commonly used to study animal behavior, such as the hibernation habits of bears or the maternal behavior of hens. It is important, however, that the subject be unaware that he is being observed. For example, a psychologist using naturalistic observation to study how children of various races play together would watch groups of children playing in the school yards or parks, but he would remain at a distance so as not to be detected. If the children noticed that a strange adult was watching, they might behave differently than they otherwise would.

questions.question:
다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
The majority of developing countries are situated in tropical or subtropical climatic zones. It is also true that the most economically successful countries are located in the temperate zone. Although social inequality and institutional factors are widely considered to be of greater importance, the division ______. The extremes of heat and humidity in most poor countries contribute to deteriorating soil quality and the rapid depreciation of many natural goods. They are also a factor in the low productivity of certain crops and the poor health of animals. Extremes of heat and humidity can also weaken workers' health, limit their desire to engage in strenuous physical work, and generally reduce their overall productivity. Furthermore, malaria and other serious parasitic diseases are often concentrated in tropical areas.
choices: ① cannot simply be attributed to coincidence
② can be easily reversed by technology
③ is mainly the result of unfair institutions
④ has nothing to do with the climate
⑤ is caused only by social inequality
questions.explanation: 이어지는 내용이 더위·습기 등 기후 요인이 빈국의 생산성 저하에 기여한다고 설명하므로, 열대/온대의 경제적 격차가 단순히 우연으로 돌릴 수 없다는 ①이 적절하다.  [출처: 절대유형 22강 22번]
questions._orig: The majority of developing countries are situated in tropical or subtropical climatic zones. It is also true that the most economically successful countries are located in the temperate zone. Although social inequality and institutional factors are widely considered to be of greater importance, the division cannot simply be attributed to coincidence. The extremes of heat and humidity in most poor countries contribute to deteriorating soil quality and the rapid depreciation of many natural goods. They are also a factor in the low productivity of certain crops, the weakened regenerative growth of forests, and the poor health of animals. Extremes of heat and humidity not only cause discomfort to workers but can also weaken their health, limit their desire to engage in strenuous physical work, and generally reduce their overall productivity and efficiency. Furthermore, malaria and other serious parasitic diseases are often concentrated in tropical areas.

questions.question:
주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
Michael Faraday, the father of electromagnetic induction, is one of history's most influential scientists.

(B) Looking back on the man's genius, Einstein said, "Faraday never went to school, and therefore preserved the rare gift of thinking freely." Einstein's view, that schooling affects creativity and genius negatively, has truth in it. The instinct of the creative genius is to explore alone and to be free to wander at will.

(A) This unique genius quality, our authenticity and originality, which is alive in every individual before schooling starts, should be recognized and constantly developed in everyone. However, this cannot erase the fact that schooling is necessary.

(C) All civilized societies require unity and widespread agreement. A school's function is to civilize and discipline people, not to create explorers. Insofar as schools demand conformity to certain patterns and structures, they threaten to undermine genius. Friction will always exist between the demands of society and the impulses of genius.
questions.explanation: Faraday 소개(주어진 글) 다음에 Einstein의 평가와 천재의 본능을 말하는 (B), 그 천재성을 길러야 하나 학교교육도 필요하다는 (A), 학교의 기능과 사회·천재의 마찰을 설명하는 (C)로 이어진다. 따라서 (B)-(A)-(C).  [출처: 절대유형 23강 24번]

However, this cannot erase the fact that schooling is necessary. All civilized societies require unity and widespread agreement. A school's function is to civilize and discipline people, not to create explorers. Insofar as schools demand conformity to certain patterns and structures, they threaten to undermine genius. Friction will always exist between the demands of society and the impulses of genius.

questions.question:
다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
As the economy expands and organizations grow accordingly, firms become even more complex, both in their tasks and in the markets they serve. Thus, the activities of individuals in these firms are necessarily becoming more specialized. An increasingly global and fast-paced economy requires people with specialized expertise. Yet the specialists within a company, whose knowledge is mostly limited to a particular part of a subject or profession, need to know how to work together. Moreover, as acquisitions, restructurings, outsourcing, and other structural changes take place, the need for coordination becomes all the more relevant. Changes in corporate structure and increases in specialization imply that there will be new boundaries between the members of an organization. These boundaries both separate and link teams within an organization, although the boundaries are not always obvious. These new relationships require team members to learn how to work with others to achieve their goals. Team members must integrate through coordination with suppliers, managers, peers, and customers.
choices: ① Growing Complexity Demands Coordination Among Specialists
② The Decline of Teamwork in the Global Economy
③ Why Specialization Harms Modern Corporations
④ Clear Boundaries: The Key to Individual Success
⑤ How Outsourcing Replaced Internal Coordination
questions.explanation: 경제가 복잡해지고 전문화가 심화될수록 전문가들 사이의 협력과 조정이 더 중요해진다는 글이므로 ①이 제목으로 적절하다.  [출처: 절대유형 25강 23번]

questions.question:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
Digital spaces — social media sites, websites, chat areas, online games, even the spaces in which we share email and text messages — are sometimes called virtual. The use of the term virtual is ① <u>misleading</u>, though, for it implies that something is almost, but not quite, ② <u>real</u>. And where digital spaces are concerned, that is simply not the case. As sociologist W. I. Thomas has classically stated, if people define situations as real, they are real in their ③ <u>consequences</u>. Digital experiences and the spaces in which they take place are quite real and have real, ④ <u>definite</u> consequences. For this reason, many consider descriptors such as sociomental, networked, and/or digital ⑤ <u>inferior</u> to virtual in describing these spaces.
choices: ① misleading
② real
③ consequences
④ definite
⑤ inferior
questions.explanation: 본문은 디지털 공간이 실재하며 실질적 결과를 가지므로, virtual이라는 표현보다 sociomental·networked·digital 같은 서술어가 더 "낫다(preferable)"고 한다. 따라서 ⑤ inferior(열등한)는 문맥상 부적절하며 preferable이 되어야 한다. ①~④는 모두 문맥상 적절하다.  [원유형: 빈칸추론→어휘 / 출처: 절대유형 13강 24번]
questions._orig: Digital spaces — social media sites, websites, chat areas, discussion boards, online games, workspaces, classes, conferences, and hangouts, even the spaces in which we share email and text messages — are sometimes called virtual. Digital work teams and organizations, in particular, are commonly described as virtual in nature. The use of the term virtual is misleading, though, for it implies that something is almost, but not quite, real. And where digital spaces are concerned, that is simply not the case. As sociologist W. I. Thomas has classically stated (in what has come to be called the Thomas Theorem), if people "define situations as real, they are real in their consequences." Digital experiences and the spaces in which they take place are quite real and have real, definite consequences. For this reason, many consider descriptors such as sociomental, networked, and/or digital preferable to virtual in describing these spaces and societies.

questions.question:
다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
Without your realizing it, others have a huge influence on almost every aspect of your life, and it goes without saying that the more you like someone, the more he or she is likely to influence you. But research by social scientists on this straightforward idea can help you become more influential in your everyday interactions. The researchers identified a range of factors, including physical attractiveness and social status, that affect how much a person will like another. Among the factors, one stood out as singularly powerful: similarity. In a simple demonstration of how this can work, researchers mailed out questionnaires. All the questionnaires were signed by a researcher, but some of the signatures were faked to make the name resemble the recipient's (e.g., Elliott Smith might receive a letter signed Dr. Elliott Simon.) Although identical in all other aspects, the questionnaires that had similar names were twice as likely to be completed and returned.
choices: ① the role of perceived similarity in shaping interpersonal influence
② the limited role of physical appearance in shaping social rank
③ methodological flaws in mail-based survey research
④ the ethical risks of manipulating identity in experiments
⑤ the human tendency to distrust those who mirror oneself
questions.explanation: 글의 핵심은 호감을 높이는 여러 요인 중 유사성이 가장 강력하며, 이름을 닮게 한 설문 회수율이 두 배였다는 실험으로 이를 입증한다. 즉 지각된 유사성이 설득의 결정적 요인이라는 ①이 적절하다. 물리적 외모·설문 방법론·실험 윤리는 부분 또는 빗나간 초점이다.

questions.question:
글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳을 고르시오.
[주어진 문장] This is a shame because every high-level concept being taught today was originally motivated by simple, common-sense principles.

Modern mathematics has been developed step by step over many centuries, which means the histories of the most recent theories can seem inaccessible to students. ( ① ) At the same time, the level of mathematical sophistication needed to grasp these theories in their final states is incredibly high. ( ② ) For exactly these reasons, math educators often make the mistake of neglecting the history of mathematical development in favor of presenting topics in their modern form. ( ③ ) While this may seem like an ideal way to give students a great deal of relevant knowledge in a short time, it leaves many students lost in a sea of remote and arbitrary abstract concepts. ( ④ ) Exposing students to this initial motivation, along with a theory's evolution, firmly places the final concept within a rational framework. ( ⑤ ) There it can then be applied correctly in practice.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '오늘날 가르치는 모든 고급 개념이 단순한 상식적 원리에서 출발했다'는 내용으로, 학생을 추상 개념의 바다에 빠뜨린다는 문제 제기(④ 앞) 뒤, 그 초기 동기를 노출시키라는 해법(④ 뒤) 앞에 와야 자연스러우므로 ④에 들어간다.  [출처: 절대유형 16강 24번]
questions._orig: Modern mathematics has been developed step by step over many centuries, which means the histories of the most recent theories — having been built upon countless prior developments — can seem inaccessible to students. At the same time, the level of mathematical sophistication needed to grasp these theories in their final states is incredibly high. For exactly these reasons, math educators often make the mistake of neglecting the history of mathematical development in favor of presenting topics in their modern form. While this may seem like an ideal way to give students a great deal of relevant knowledge in a short time, it leaves many students lost in a sea of remote and arbitrary abstract concepts. This is a shame because every high-level concept being taught today was originally motivated by simple, common-sense principles. Exposing students to this initial motivation, along with a theory's evolution, firmly places the final concept within a rational framework, where it can then be applied correctly in practice.

questions.question:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
We all want to believe that our brains sort through information in the most rational way possible. On the contrary, countless studies by psychologists, educators, and neurobiologists show that there are many issues with human reasoning. For example, confirmation bias is ubiquitous. People pay attention to information that supports their viewpoints, while ignoring evidence to the contrary. Confirmation bias is not the same as being stubborn, and is not constrained to issues about which people have strong opinions. Instead, it acts at a subconscious level controlling how we gather and filter information. Most of us are not aware of these types of flaws in our reasoning processes, but professionals who work to convince us of certain viewpoints study the research on human decision making to determine how to exploit our weaknesses to make us more susceptible to their messages. Becoming more aware of our own vulnerabilities inhibits their efforts.

⇩
Human reasoning is systematically (A) by tendencies such as confirmation bias, but becoming (B) of these flaws can reduce others' attempts to exploit them.
choices: ① (A) protected … (B) unaware
② (A) distorted … (B) ignorant
③ (A) improved … (B) aware
④ (A) guided … (B) afraid
⑤ (A) distorted … (B) aware
questions.explanation: 인간의 추론은 확증편향 같은 경향에 의해 왜곡(distorted)되지만, 그 결함을 인식(aware)하면 이를 악용하려는 시도를 줄일 수 있다는 내용이므로 ⑤가 적절하다.  [출처: 절대유형 24강 24번]

On the contrary, countless studies by psychologists, educators, and neurobiologists show that there are many issues with human reasoning. For example, confirmation bias is ubiquitous. Confirmation bias is not the same as being stubborn, and is not constrained to issues about which people have strong opinions. Instead, it acts at a subconscious level controlling how we gather and filter information. Most of us are not aware of these types of flaws in our reasoning processes, but professionals who work to convince us of certain viewpoints study the research on human decision making to determine how to exploit our weaknesses to make us more susceptible to their messages. Becoming more aware of our own vulnerabilities inhibits their efforts.

questions.question:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
With the modern-day explosion of the self-improvement phenomenon, we hear over and over again how important it is to have high self-esteem. Believe in yourself, all the self-help experts say, and you will easily succeed. But for many people, the ①<u>reverse</u> is the recipe for their personal success. These people achieve recognition and fulfillment not because of their supposed stores of self-belief but because of their acute ②<u>fears</u> of failure. Feelings of inadequacy ③<u>force</u> these people to prove themselves capable of great things. This was the view of the famed critic Edmund Wilson, who cited Karl Marx and Edna St. Vincent Millay as two people whose fears of failure forced them to work harder and never give up. The bottom line is that the fear of failure keeps us from ④<u>settling</u> for "good enough." And not settling is ⑤<u>irrelevant</u> to success.
questions.explanation: 마지막 문장은 '안주하지 않는 것이 성공에 필수적(essential)'이라는 흐름이므로 irrelevant(무관한)는 부적절하다. ①reverse, ②fears, ③force, ④settling은 모두 적절.  [출처: 절대유형 11강 22번]
questions._orig: With the modern-day explosion of the self-improvement phenomenon, we hear over and over again how important it is to have high self-esteem. Believe in yourself, all the self-help experts say, and you will easily succeed. But for many people, the reverse is the recipe for their personal success. These people achieve recognition and fulfillment not because of their supposed stores of self-belief but because of their acute fears of failure. Feelings of inadequacy force these people to prove themselves capable of great things. This was the view of the famed writer and critic Edmund Wilson, who cited the philosopher Karl Marx and the poet Edna St. Vincent Millay as two people whose fears of failure forced them to work harder and harder and never give up. The bottom line is that the fear of failure keeps us from settling for "good enough." And not settling is essential to success.

questions.question:
다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
Whenever a youngster rescues himself from boredom by generating his own amusements, it strengthens his feelings of self-worth and boosts his overall confidence in his ability to solve problems. ① Another significant advantage is that children who learn to cope with boredom tend to do better in situations that involve extended periods of waiting. ② Children who have developed their own private resources tend to be less restless, demanding, and stressed when they have to tolerate tedious delays. ③ Parents should therefore enroll their children in as many structured after-school programs as possible to keep them constantly occupied. ④ Finally, boredom is often the "trigger" for daydreaming, and the capacity to be alone becomes linked with self-discovery and self-realization. ⑤ We may be sure that such moments do not occur when the child is playing football, but rather when he is on his own.
questions.explanation: 글 전체는 아이가 스스로 지루함을 다루며 자기효능감·자기발견을 키운다는 내용이다. ③은 구조화된 프로그램으로 끊임없이 바쁘게 하라는 정반대 주장으로 전체 흐름과 무관하다.  [출처: 절대유형 12강 24번]
questions._orig: Whenever a youngster rescues himself from boredom by generating his own amusements, it strengthens his feelings of self-worth and boosts his overall confidence in his ability to solve problems. Another significant advantage is that children who learn to cope with boredom tend to do better in situations that involve extended periods of waiting. Children who have developed their own private resources — who have learned to occupy their time with games of make-believe and imagination — tend to be less restless, demanding, and stressed when they have to tolerate tedious delays and waits. Finally, boredom is often the "trigger" for daydreaming. The capacity to be alone thus becomes linked with self-discovery and self-realization — with becoming aware of our deepest needs, feelings, and impulses. We may be sure that such moments do not occur when the child is playing football, but rather when he is on his own.

questions.question:
밑줄 친 <u>there is no such thing as society</u>가 다음 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
Former Prime Minister of the United Kingdom Margaret Thatcher declared that <u>there is no such thing as society</u>. In that context, "society" is the same as "government". She made the point that no government can do anything except through people, and people must look to themselves first and then look after their neighbor. Political theorists use the term "social capital" to describe the wealth of trust and reciprocity created within social groups. We build norms, rules, and relations that enable us to cooperate with and depend upon one another. Consider communities that are low on income but high on social capital. People in Uganda could improve rural healthcare dramatically simply by creating a renewed sense of social contract backed up with public accountability.
choices: ① Society does not exist because people are fundamentally selfish.
② Governments should completely replace social communities.
③ Social problems can only be solved by increasing national income.
④ Government cannot act on its own; people must take responsibility for themselves and others.
⑤ Individuals have no obligation to care for their neighbors.
questions.explanation: Thatcher의 말은 사회가 곧 정부이며 정부는 사람을 통해서만 작동하므로 사람들이 스스로와 이웃을 먼저 돌봐야 한다는 의미이다. 따라서 ④가 적절하다.  [출처: 절대유형 22강 24번]
questions._orig: Former Prime Minister of the United Kingdom Margaret Thatcher declared that there is no such thing as society. In that context, "society" is the same as "government". She made the point that no government can do anything except through people, and people must look to themselves first and then look after their neighbor. Political theorists use the term "social capital" to describe the wealth of trust and reciprocity that is created within social groups as a result of their networks or relationships. We build norms, rules, and relations that enable us to cooperate with and depend upon one another. These connections build social cohesion and help meet our fundamental human needs, such as participation, leisure, protection and belonging. And it can motivate us by far more than cost and price. Consider communities that are low on income but high on social capital. People in Uganda, for example, could improve the quality and quantity of rural healthcare dramatically simply by creating a renewed sense of social contract backed up with public accountability such as involving local members in monitoring clinic management and decision making.

questions.question:
다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
You need to change the lens through which you observe and interpret our increasingly interdependent world. You can neither capture nor appreciate the full richness and complexity of the physical world if you only take snapshots using a still camera. Rather, you need to train your mind to act as a sophisticated "mental camera" to gain ______ of the rapidly-changing world. For example, a still picture of Usain Bolt sprinting in a 100m race won't unveil his sheer velocity; but a 10-second video will do justice to his lightning-speed performance.
choices: ① a dynamic view
② a fixed image
③ a simpler explanation
④ a permanent record
⑤ an emotional distance
questions.explanation: 정지 사진과 대비해 10초짜리 영상이 속도를 제대로 보여주듯, 빠르게 변하는 세계를 역동적 시각(dynamic view)으로 봐야 한다는 내용이므로 ①이 적절하다.  [출처: 절대유형 15강 21번]
questions._orig: You need to change the lens through which you observe and interpret our increasingly interdependent world — a world that's getting more and more complicated every day. You can neither capture nor appreciate the full richness and complexity of the physical world if you only take snapshots using a still camera. Rather, you need to train your mind to act as a sophisticated "mental camera" to gain a dynamic view of the rapidly-changing world. For example, a still picture of Usain Bolt sprinting in a 100m race won't unveil his sheer velocity; but a 10-second video will do justice to his lightning-speed performance. Fortunately, in today's fast-paced digital-information environment, it's easier for us to form opinions and make decisions based on a dynamic view of an issue as we have access to more information.

questions.question:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
In 1883, Francis Galton, cousin of the famous biologist Charles Darwin, came up with a new, unique technique called composite photography, which he believed could be used to identify different "types" of people based solely on their physical appearance. To prove his belief, he created photographic composite images of the faces of vegetarians and criminals, which were used to see if there was a typical facial appearance for each. While the resultant "averaged" faces did little to allow the identification of either criminals or vegetarians, Galton observed that the mixed images were more attractive than any of the individual images. A group of researchers reproduced the result under more controlled conditions and found that the computer-made, mathematical average of a series of faces is rated more favorably than individual faces.
⇩
Galton's composite photography proved (A)____ as a tool for categorization, yet it incidentally exposed an aesthetic preference for the (B)____ over the distinctive.
choices: ① futile ··· exceptional
② futile ··· prototypical
③ controversial ··· prototypical
④ decisive ··· conventional
⑤ controversial ··· anomalous
questions.explanation: 골턴의 합성사진은 얼굴 유형으로 사람을 분류하는 데는 실패(futile)했지만, 평균화된 전형적(prototypical) 얼굴이 개별 얼굴보다 더 매력적으로 평가된다는 점을 우연히 드러냈다. (A)=futile, (B)=prototypical이므로 ②가 적절하다.  [원유형: 제목→요약문완성 / 출처: 절대유형 16강 22번]
questions._orig: In 1883, Francis Galton, cousin of the famous biologist Charles Darwin, came up with a new, unique technique called composite photography, which he believed could be used to identify different "types" of people based solely on their physical appearance. To prove his belief, he created photographic composite images of the faces of vegetarians and criminals, which were used to see if there was a typical facial appearance for each. While the resultant "averaged" faces did little to allow the identification of either criminals or vegetarians, Galton observed he noticed that the mixed images were more attractive than any of the individual images. A group of researchers reproduced the result under more controlled conditions and found that the computer-made, mathematical average of a series of faces is rated more favorably than individual faces.

questions.question:
다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
Harp and Mayer performed an experiment about how adding visuals and text that are topically related to a lesson but irrelevant to the learning goal affects learning. They created two versions of a lesson teaching the process of lightning formation. The basic version used words and relevant visuals. The enhanced version added short narrative vignettes such as a video of lightning striking trees and an ambulance arriving, while the narrator said: "Approximately 10,000 Americans are injured by lightning every year." Learning was about 30 percent better for students using the basic lesson version. The enhancements actually ______ because they stole attention from the primary content aligned with the learning goal.
choices: ① improved long-term memory
② doubled student motivation
③ clarified the main concept
④ had no measurable effect
⑤ detracted from learning
questions.explanation: 기본형 학습이 30% 더 효과적이었고 흥미로운 추가 요소가 핵심 내용에서 주의를 빼앗았다고 했으므로, 그 향상 요소가 오히려 학습을 저해했다(detracted from learning)는 ⑤가 적절하다.  [출처: 절대유형 21강 23번]
questions._orig: Harp and Mayer performed an experiment about how adding visuals and text that are topically related to a lesson but irrelevant to the learning goal affects learning. They created two versions of a lesson that taught the process of lightning formation. The basic lesson version used words and relevant visuals to describe the process. The enhanced lesson version added short narrative vignettes with visuals such as a video of lightning striking trees, an ambulance arriving near the trees, and a lightning victim being carried on a stretcher to the ambulance. At the same time, the narrator said: "Approximately 10,000 Americans are injured by lightning every year." Learning was about 30 percent better for students using the basic lesson version. The enhancements actually detracted from learning because they stole attention from the primary content aligned with the learning goal.

questions.question:
다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [4.1점]
Research on the universality of facial expressions suggests that the socialization of affect involves interactions between situational variables and a finite repertoire of human emotions whose meanings are at least roughly synonymous among all members of the species. At the same time, Izard's formulation of "affective-cognitive structures" shows that emotions are in reality not separable from the particular circumstances that are associated with them. The fact that it is possible to construct a list of "basic," universally recognizable emotions derives not only from a species-specific repertoire of facial expressions, but perhaps more fundamentally from a larger set of human expressive behaviors, including laughter and crying as well as bodily movements and postures. These behaviors, for which a universal capacity exists, are also, without exception, carried out in particular circumstances. As elements in the human communicative function, they create the necessity of response from the environment while also being shaped by it. To use Lewis's terms, the contextual reality of emotional expression ______.
choices: ① confirms that affective meaning precedes the situations that elicit it
② converts a latent biological state into a situated lived experience
③ reduces the universal repertoire to a set of culturally fixed codes
④ isolates innate expression from the demands of social interaction
⑤ subordinates situational variation to a finite catalogue of emotions
questions.explanation: 밑줄 명제는 감정 표현의 맥락적 실재가 잠재적 상태를 상황 속 경험으로 전환한다는 뜻이다(state→experience). 따라서 ②. ②는 인과 방향이 반대, ③⑤는 보편 레퍼토리를 고정·종속으로 왜곡, ④는 환경과의 상호 형성을 분리로 뒤집은 오답이다.  [출처: 수특영독 1강 1번]
questions._orig: Research on the universality of facial expressions...

questions.question:
주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오. [3.6점]
Recognizing changes in the natural world caused in part or entirely due to human activities ─ such as climate change, pollution and habitat loss ─ tourists are pursuing what is referred to as 'last chance' tourism, travel motivated by the desire to see threatened or diminishing natural attractions such as glaciers, coral reefs and endangered species.

(A) Over-tourism describes the tipping point where the costs of tourism outweigh the benefits for local communities due to overcrowding or poor management. If not managed properly, it is a threat to sustainable tourism development.

(B) Locations featuring these attractions may continue to experience heightened visitation, simultaneously creating opportunities for increased awareness and resource protection as well as increased risk of over-tourism. Over-tourism is acknowledged as a major threat to the industry.

(C) The growing concern for it offers opportunities for tourism professionals to implement sustainability best practices. It calls upon destination managers to engage with all sectors and stakeholders towards long-term, fact-based planning to mitigate over-tourism.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글(last chance tourism 정의) → (B) 방문 증가의 양면과 over-tourism 등장 → (A) over-tourism 정의·위협 → (C) 지속가능 관리 해법 결론. 따라서 (B)-(A)-(C), ③.  [출처: 수특영독 8강 4번]
questions._orig: last chance tourism...

questions.question:
다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [4점]
Across different performance domains, successful performance is not just dependent on proficient movement control and the successful execution of skills; often effective decision-making is also a core requirement. ① Decision-making can generally be viewed as the process of committing to a particular course of action when a number of options are available to the performer. ② The decisions that are made are influenced by past experiences and the knowledge base the individual performer has of the specific situation. ③ Physical fitness programs therefore prioritize muscular endurance over cognitive preparation in most elite sports. ④ There is often more than one right decision, and the 'right' decision will often differ from individual to individual depending upon their skill level and expertise. ⑤ The timescale within which a decision is made also varies, as does the underpinning explanation of the process, which differs depending on whether the decision is time-constrained or not.
choices: ①
②
③
④
⑤
questions.explanation: 글은 수행에서 의사결정이라는 인지 과정의 특성(선택·과거경험 영향·복수 정답·시간 제약)을 논한다. ③은 체력 훈련이 인지 준비보다 근지구력을 우선한다는 내용으로 의사결정 논점과 무관하다. 따라서 ③.  [출처: 수특영독 6강 10번]
questions._orig: Across different performance domains...

questions.question:
다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [4.2점]
Procedures have recently been developed that separate imitation from other forms of social influence and social learning, and the results of initial studies indicate that species from chimpanzees to quail can imitate. Such findings should not be surprising because social learning, whether by imitation or some other process, often provides greater benefits than genetically predisposed behavior or trial-and-error learning. However, the processes involved that enable animals to match their behavior to that of a demonstrator are poorly understood. Imitation may involve some form of coordination of visual and touch-based sensory modalities, perspective taking, or response facilitation, but the role of such processes in opaque imitation is still unknown. A reasonable strategy would be to determine the necessary and sufficient conditions for opaque imitation to occur. Finally, the ability to learn from others may not only make the acquisition of survival behavior more efficient but may also free the animal from trial-and-error learning to engage in innovative variants that may be adopted by others.
choices: ① Why Trial-and-Error Learning Outperforms Social Imitation
② Genetic Predisposition as the Sole Basis of Animal Behavior
③ The Proven Sensory Steps Behind Every Act of Imitation
④ Imitation in Animals: Evidence, Unknown Mechanisms, and Adaptive Value
⑤ How Imitation Ultimately Limits Innovation Across Species
questions.explanation: 글은 동물 모방의 증거(침팬지~메추라기), 아직 규명되지 않은 메커니즘, 그리고 적응적 가치(혁신 촉진)를 함께 다룬다. 따라서 ④. ②③은 본문이 부정하거나 반대, ④는 "proven"이 본문(poorly understood)과 모순, ⑤는 본문과 정반대이다.  [출처: 수특영독 6강 4번]
questions._orig: Procedures have recently been developed...

questions.question:
밑줄 친 <u>the white supremacy embedded in standard practices</u>가 다음 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.6점]
American educators saw Asian American parenting as deviant and, correspondingly, felt white middle class parents and kids set an appropriate standard that others should conform to. For example, when white children outperform minority students, teachers rarely see it as 'academic bullying.' Whites are not expected to emulate those who achieve more, whereas black and Latinx youths are. Also, teachers, predominantly white, reinforce a 'hidden curriculum' ─ informal norms for what constitutes proper behavior, dress, attitudes, and discipline in schools. Racial inequalities arise even in integrated and reasonably resourced schools. Educators make significant efforts to address the learning gaps facing minority youths but do not disrupt <u>the white supremacy embedded in standard practices</u>. The taken-for-granted assumption that white students' practices are 'normal' contributes to why Asian Americans are framed as 'deviant.'
choices: ① the unspoken assumption that white students' norms define what counts as normal
② an explicit policy that openly favors white students over all minorities
③ the deliberate exclusion of minority families from school funding
④ a temporary bias that disappears in well-resourced integrated schools
⑤ the belief that academic ability is determined entirely by race
questions.explanation: 밑줄은 백인 학생의 관행을 '정상'으로 보는 암묵적 전제가 학교의 표준 관행에 내재해 있음을 뜻한다(hidden curriculum). 따라서 ①. ②는 explicit(본문은 암묵적), ④는 본문이 부정(통합학교에서도 발생), ③⑤는 본문에 없거나 과장이다.  [출처: 수특영독 7강 3번]
questions._orig: American educators saw Asian American parenting...

questions.question:
글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳을 고르시오. [3.6점]
[주어진 문장] Yet this zoo of data is still insufficient to provide a holistic description of this pervasive phenomenon.

Marine plastic pollution is a complex problem that occurs on many levels, as it presents physical, chemical, and biological implications for marine compartments at small scales while involving vast geographic domains. ( ① ) To counteract what can be regarded as a planetary boundary threat, we need tailored instruments to provide various layers of knowledge in an accessible manner. ( ② ) To this end, laboratory experiments and observations are indeed fundamental to capture specific aspects of plastic and plastic-related pollution. ( ③ ) Quantitative methods can link and exploit our current understanding of the different processes and complex interactions to shed some light on aspects that are hard to investigate in the field. ( ④ ) Actions against marine pollution have to be timely, bold, and knowledge-based. ( ⑤ )
choices: ①
②
③
④
⑤
questions.explanation: 실험·관찰이 기본이라는 ②뒤 문장에 이어, 주어진 문장(그러나 이 데이터 더미만으로는 전체를 기술하기에 불충분)이 한계를 지적하고, 그 한계를 보완하는 정량적 방법(③뒤)으로 자연스럽게 연결된다. 따라서 ③.  [출처: 수특영독 7강 4번]
questions._orig: Marine plastic pollution is a complex problem...

questions.question:
[27-28] 다음 글을 읽고, 물음에 답하시오.
Grice, a British philosopher of language, proposed that, in addition to communicative meaning, there is another kind of meaning, which he referred to as natural meaning, characterized by 'things' that have meaning regardless of whether there is any communicative intention on anyone's part. For example, I have learned that dynamite means danger. Thus, if I find a box of dynamite in my garage, dynamite means danger to me and I am going to be frightened. To recognize the danger, it is not necessary for me to recognize that someone intentionally placed the dynamite there with the intention of getting me to recognize that dynamite is dangerous; that is, it is not necessary that I recognize any communicative intention behind the box being there to recognize danger. And, further, even if the dynamite had been put there with the intention of getting me to recognize I was in danger, it would not be necessary for me to recognize that in order to feel in danger. Simply put, the word 'dynamite' on a box means danger whether or not anyone intended to have me recognize that meaning.

27. 윗글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?

③ Two Kinds of Meaning: Intended Versus Inherent
④ Why Context Determines the Meaning of Any Sign
